Ostrow Mazowiecka New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ostrów Mazowiecka, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Ostrów Mazowiecka is confirmed from the 18th century; Rabbi Jehoszua (from 1843) and rabbis Gerszon Henoch Leiner and Bencijon Rabinowicz were all connected to the town. By 1921, 6,812 (50%) endured German killings of about 300 Jews in September 1939, followed by a further 300-800 shot on November 11 that year, with survivors forced to leave; a 1947 Jewish Committee registered 23 people. This cemetery, likely established between 1871-1925, was formally closed on October 9, 1964, with documentation noting it had been closed since 1939 and remained unfenced and overgrown.
